evidence_items.locator: Introduction, paragraph beginning 'It’s only been a year and a half'
evidence_items.explanation: Supports the comparable-software component. The evaluation section compares Meta's vision models with GPT4o-mini, but these are Meta's own evaluations and do not establish the absence of an OpenAI moat.

Section 1(a) grants royalty-free rights to use and modify the defined materials. Attribution, acceptable-use rules, and separate authorization for licensees exceeding 700 million monthly active users qualify what free means.

evidence_items.locator: Opening discussion of the Llama 3.1 release
evidence_items.explanation: Documents free distribution before September, while also discussing commercial restrictions and capability differences. It is context because the release predates the target period.

evidence_items.locator: Introduction, first paragraph describing the new models
evidence_items.explanation: OpenAI's reasoning-model release is material evidence of differentiation. Its company-reported improvements over previous models neither measure durability nor establish superiority over all competitors.

unresolved_gaps: The sources do not establish whether OpenAI's technical, distribution, brand, or customer advantages constituted durable barriers in September 2024.
Comparable Meta models and royalty-free licensing do not by themselves establish the absence of a moat.
No speaker-supplied standard determines when a competitive advantage becomes an obvious moat.
